# Storyboard: The Warrior Counts

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/warrior.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

The Warrior Counts are not a chapter: no choices, one sitting of 55 questions, every pair up to ten times ten once, and the frames around it (`PC.warrior`, docs/warrior-counts.md). Each frame is boarded as a chapter’s is (**Shot**, **Scene**, **Captions**, **Balloons**, **Then**). The opening’s frames and the result’s are played in order with Next and the big Back beside it; a result page that depends on how the sitting went is listed with each of its versions.

`{name}` is the first part of her Clan name, `{petname}` what her Tall One calls her, and `{Murmur}`/`{murmur}` the tortoiseshell’s name word (Murmur, or Mutter for a reader whose own Clan name is Murmur). The result’s own words come first, in number words: `{right}`/`{Right}` her right answers, `{last}`/`{Last}` her last finished sitting’s, `{short}` fifty less `{right}`, and `{tricky}` the one or two Counts her misses fall in (“the 7s and the 8s”); a capital starts a sentence.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Opens | once `ch10` is finished, from the hub’s big button (never the Training Hollow); after the pass, a quiet “The Warrior Counts again” |
| A sitting | 55 questions, 10 × 10 always last; 50 right passes; a miss gets the sand’s help once and is not asked again; four paw prints, no score, no clock |
| Frames | 23 (the openings 6, halfway 1, the pass 5, the not-yet 8, after the pass 3) |
| Captions and balloons | 11 captions, 27 balloons, about 359 words in all |
| Scenes | camp 22 · tower 1 |

## The hub

Once `ch10` is finished the big button is the Warrior Counts’ until she passes, and no chapter’s “coming soon” shows:

- a result she has not seen to its last button: **The Warrior Counts** / *Glintstar is waiting* (it opens the result again);
- never sat: **The Warrior Counts** / *When you’re ready*;
- a sitting to pick up (an answer in it, within two hours of when she was last there, nothing practiced since): **Keep going** / *The Warrior Counts · third paw*;
- after a not-yet: **The Warrior Counts** / *Try again whenever you like*;
- passed: the Ceremony’s chapter button, as any chapter’s, and under it, quietly, **The Warrior Counts again**; while the Ceremony is not built, “Your ceremony is coming soon.” in its place, here and in her book. A sitting again whose result she has not seen waits in the quiet slot, **The Warrior Counts: Glintstar is waiting**, and the Ceremony keeps the big one.

## The question panel

**Scene.** Camp: CrystalClan’s camp, the wild garden behind the hedge, in the morning (bramble dens, ferns, mossy stone paths, a dry stone fountain, glass towers all around). Camera: the cats, staring (`crowd`). Cast: Glintstar (sitting, on top of the fountain, facing left); you (sitting, at a spot of this frame’s own (x 760, y 860), facing right); Tallyheart (sitting, kind, at a spot of this frame’s own (x 950, y 872), facing left); Murmurchime, the tortoiseshell warrior (sitting, happy, in the crowd, right, facing left). Also: the whole Clan crowded round the fountain, rows of cats behind. Effects: morning light, washed clean after the storm.

The same panel for all 55. It is drawn with the crowd until she has a finished sitting; after that the camp is quiet: the same panel without the crowd (the halfway page too).

Under the panel Glintstar asks each question in her balloon, in words (“Seven times eight.”), then the question line in Andika (“7 × 8 = ?”) and the keypad. Above the question line, four paw prints, one a quarter (14, 14, 14 and 13 questions): the one she is on fills a little at every answer, a miss the same as a right one. Read to me says Glintstar’s balloon, not the question line. On a miss the panel turns to Tallyheart’s sand, the count scratched out in the pair’s anchor Count’s way.

**The last question, 10 × 10:**

- *Caption*: At last:
- **Glintstar**: “Ten times ten.”

**Right:**

- **You**, shouting: “A HUNDRED!”

**Missed:** the sand, then Tallyheart: “There. A hundred. And that’s every Count!”

### When the sitting before was set aside

Tallyheart says why, once, at the start of her balloon on that one panel, before “Every Count, same as before.” (also when the sitting before was opened and left with no answer, which is dropped, not recorded; never on the first opening):

- two hours went by (`late`): “It’s been a while, so we start fresh.”
- she practiced other Counts in between (`practice`): “You’ve been practicing, so we start fresh.”

### A sitting picked up

Within two hours of when she was last there, with nothing practiced since, it picks up at the same question, under:

- **Tallyheart**: “Where were we? Ah, yes.”

(A sitting picked up before its first answer plays its own opening again.)

## The sitting

Tallyheart’s lines (Glintstar asks every question):

- After a right answer, now and then (4 of the 20 praise entries say something; a blank says nothing and the next question comes): “Yes.”, “Good.”, “That’s it.”, “Steady paws.”. Quick ones: “Quick as a pounce!”, “Snap! Just like that.”, “Fast as a sparrow.”, “Sure and quick.”.
- Right on one of her hard facts, every other one, in turn (4 lines, a blank between): quick, “Last time, {a} × {b} made you stop and think. Not today!”, “{a} × {b}! That one used to be tricky.”, “No stopping on {a} × {b} this time.”, “Quick! {a} × {b} used to take a while.”; slow, “{a} × {b} again, and you got it. It’s getting easier.”, “You worked out {a} × {b}. Good.”, “{a} × {b} was tricky last time. You got it.”, “{a} × {b}. It gets easier every time.”. A long line stays until it is read (about 0.4 s a word) or said to its end.
- After a miss, in turn, never one twice running: “There. Now you’ve seen it. On we go.”, “That’s a tricky one. On to the next.”, “There it is. You’re doing fine. Keep going.”, “Now it’s in the sand. On we go.”.
- No line after a miss for the right answers that follow (no `fastAfterMiss`), and none that counts what is left.

### The pauses

- After the 14th answer, Tallyheart: “One paw done. Your whiskers are wide awake now.”
- After the 42nd answer, Tallyheart: “Three paws done. Just one more paw.”

Each stays 2.5 s, or 3.5 s when its line is over six words, or as long as its words take to read (0.6 s and 0.38 s a word) when that is longer (with Read to me on, until it has been said, and half a second more; at most that long again after that); a tap moves on. No Back: a pause comes after an answer. A sitting picked up right at a pause says “Where were we? Ah, yes.” in it, first, and the pause waits for all of it.
